decisions.reason: As a recently launched core cardboard display with an adjustable feature, it fits the firm's main POS portfolio and is likely to be retained while demand is tested.
The pegboard-back shelf display is a standard retail-display variant within the firm's core competence, so a large manufacturer would usually keep it on offer after only one year.
Although it overlaps with other quarter-pallet formats, it is still a mainstream corrugated display product and likely worth keeping as a basic option.
The eighth-pallet format serves a distinct smaller-footprint retail need, making early withdrawal less likely for a large display producer.
A wooden display pallet sits less naturally in a paper-products firm's core range, so management would be relatively more likely to discontinue it and refocus on corrugated solutions.
It is somewhat exposed to a narrower media-products niche, but as a cardboard quarter-pallet display it still broadly matches the firm's established display business.
